message.content:
The “best” movie of 2020 is a matter of taste and criteria, but if you look at critical consensus, audience reception, and award recognition, **“Nomadland”** often comes out on top.

| Why “Nomadland” stands out | Details |
|----------------------------|---------|
| **Critical acclaim** | 94 % on Rotten Tomatoes (fresh) and 87 % on Metacritic. |
| **Audience reception** | 8.2/10 on IMDb, 4.5/5 on Letterboxd. |
| **Awards** | Won the Academy Award for Best Picture, Best Director (Chloé Zhao), and Best Actress (Frances McDormand). It also swept the Golden Globes for Best Motion Picture – Drama and Best Director. |
| **Cultural impact** | Sparked conversations about the gig economy, rural America, and the definition of “home.” |
| **Unique storytelling** | A quiet, contemplative narrative that blends documentary realism with a fictional arc, featuring a real-life nomad (Frances McDormand) and a cast of non‑actors. |

Other strong contenders from 2020 include:

| Film | Highlights |
|------|------------|
| **“Parasite”** | Though released in 2019, it dominated the 2020 awards season, winning Best Picture at the Oscars and sweeping the BAFTAs. |
| **“Soul”** | Pixar’s Oscar‑winning animated film that won Best Animated Feature and Best Original Score. |
| **“The Trial of the Chicago 7”** | 100 % on Rotten Tomatoes, praised for its sharp political drama. |
| **“The Father”** | Won Best Actor (Anthony Hopkins) and Best Supporting Actress (Olivia Colman) at the Oscars. |

If you’re looking for a film that combined critical praise, audience love, and major awards, **“Nomadland”** is the most celebrated movie of 2020.
